analysis.title: GS Arruda - What Matters Today: Privo Resilient. AI on the watch. Positioning is a tailwind, Fed is a headwind, US Econ Adding a Third Hike in March, China Where to Find Growth? 11 Nov 2026
key_insights: SPX barely fell on 11/10 and futures are recovering this morning. AI sentiment appears to be improving. Even after a hot CPI print the market could not sustain the volatility premium: VIX briefly traded into the 20s but closed below 20.

GS argues positioning is now doing more to support the tape than macro is doing to undermine it. Net exposure is historically low, gross has been cut, and investors are heavily hedged, which GS calls the tailwind for the tape.

Neocloud commentary overnight was broadly supportive. Data center capacity constraints remain the main operational bottleneck, and compute utilization across major providers is elevated. Market focus is on hardware delivery and developer coding workflows, while edge and enterprise autonomous integrations are at an earlier stage.

Rates are a headwind, but the prior rally built a cushion, so rates are not yet a red flag for equities. GS says yields need another leg higher before they become a material problem, and that the rate of change matters most.
Credit is the area GS flags to watch, with high yield spreads chopping sideways. GS also notes cyclicality relative to the market is holding in.

GS describes an energy reflexivity loop: higher oil, stickier inflation, a more hawkish Fed. The open question is whether the Fed is reacting to energy effects already in the past or to something more persistent.
GS says volatility remains elevated relative to price action and that, absent fresh negative information, the premium should keep decaying.
US Veterans Day on 11/11: the bond market is closed and equities are open. GS is watching the neoclouds and the next move in energy.
GS US Economics says October CPI surprised meaningfully to the upside across several categories and was a third straight month of worse inflation news.

GS expects a second 25bp hike in December and has added a third 25bp hike in March 2027. A January hike is possible, but March is more likely because November and December inflation should be softer and January should see larger start-of-year price increases.

GS says oil futures have fallen substantially since the elections, so most of the energy-shock passthrough to consumer prices should be behind. GS remains confident inflation will be meaningfully lower by end-2027 as tariff, energy and AI price pressures fade.

GS expects most FOMC participants to signal a third hike in the December dot plot. A firmer January inflation report would make delivering it the path of least resistance even if the energy shock has ended by then.
GS left its terminal fed funds forecast unchanged at 3.25-3.5%, but now expects cuts to begin in December 2027 (previously September 2027), followed by cuts in March, June and September 2028.

China: US$5tn of GDP has been added since Covid, but Chinese stocks have not converted that growth into equity returns. GS points to factors that have suppressed the cost of capital for Chinese corporates, and says the growth equity universe has become more concentrated.
GS forecasts 10% trend EPS growth and 12% normal ROE for Chinese stocks over the next 5 years.

GS stays strategically bullish on structural AI and 'Going Global' growth, meaning AI tech hardware and export-oriented sectors. It cites strong near-term earnings momentum and a significant de-rating in the recent drawdown in AI proxies, and would use weakness to build positions.

GS says the group looks well positioned while US rates rise and China rates fall, and while US-China yield spreads stay wide. It favors earnings turnarounds and cash flow in de-rated and cyclical growth, and avoids depressed growth until housing stabilizes.

For a more conservative way to go long China, GS has seen interest in floored swaps on the CSI300. Tech is almost 30% of the index, almost double its weight at the start of 2025. Funding levels make buying puts closer to ATM cheaper.

tension_points.bull_case: Positioning is a tailwind: nets are historically low, gross has been cut and investors are heavily hedged, so the market held up after a hot CPI print and the VIX closed below 20.
tension_points.bear_case: The Fed is a headwind: October CPI was a third month of worse inflation news, GS now sees hikes in December and March, and higher oil could keep inflation sticky. Credit spreads are the area to watch.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Yields need another leg higher before they become a material problem for equities, and fresh negative information would stop the volatility premium from decaying.
